title: A077754 - Murthy's conjecture: prescribed digit sums in residue classes (Lean 4)
description: Machine-checked proof of theorem A077754 (conjecture of Amarnath Murthy, OEIS, 2002): for every n, there exists a multiple N of n with all-nonzero digits, digit sum n and at least 2 digits, iff n is not in {1,2,5,11} and not divisible by 10. Unconditional, proved for all n. NEW IN v8: the OEIS sequence value itself is formalized in module A077754Val - a077754_val n is certified IsLeast of the admissible multiples for every non-exceptional n (the 'smallest multiple ... or 0 if no such multiple exists' clause of the entry, previously not formalized), a(n)=0 iff n in {1,2,5,11} or 10|n, and the displayed terms are kernel-certified value anchors with minimality (a(3)=12, a(4)=112, a(6)=24, a(7)=133, a(8)=152, a(9)=18, a(12)=48; zeros at n=1,2,5,10,11,20,30,40). Trust base: the Lean kernel alone - #print axioms = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] on theorem A077754 and on all A077754Val theorems; every finite certificate is kernel-checked by decide (bitmap certificates in A077754Cert.lean); no native_decide, no sorryAx.
